meaning: Name of the state variable: Cho_Cr, NAA_Cr or roi_volume.
Unit of the variable. 1 means a ratio without unit; mm3 is cubic millimetres.
The twin's best value for the variable right now (posterior mean).
How unsure the twin is, as a variance. Its square root is the error bar.
Standard deviation of the belief: the plus-or-minus shown on screen.
Time of the latest evidence used, in months since the baseline session.
initialized, updated or updated_with_warning.
Baseline value that later values are compared with in the change test.
Standard uncertainty of the baseline value.
Packet that set the baseline.
Session of the baseline packet.
Every packet that has moved this variable, in order. Used to block double counting.
Every session that has moved this variable. One packet per session per variable.
Running number of the event in the append-only log.
When the twin processed the packet (server clock, not the scan time).
Twin version after this event. Every event, including a reject, adds one.
Decision taken: initialize, update, update_with_warning or reject.
Identifier of the evidence packet this event used.
Which variable the packet measures.
Pseudonymous session label of the packet.
Time of the evidence in months since baseline, checked against the sessions table.
Effective quality status after all six check layers: PASS, WARN or FAIL. Never better than the packet's own worst check.
One-sentence verdict shown on screen.
All findings of the six-layer check (see the finding.* fields).
Path of the source file inside the StarterPack.
SHA-256 fingerprint of the source file.
True when the fingerprint was recomputed from the file and matched. Says the bytes are unchanged, not that the physics is right.
Parents (source files) and activities (processing steps) declared by the packet.
Pipeline name, version and fit method that produced the value.
Origin of the underlying data: SIMULATED or MEASURED. Here always SIMULATED.
Epistemic label of the packet value, for example DERIVED.
Epistemic label of the decision itself. Always INFERRED.
The measured value in the packet.
Uncertainty as stated by the packet, converted to a standard deviation.
Uncertainty the twin actually uses. Larger than stated when the stated one is too optimistic (region volume rule).
Packet variance, u_effective squared. Always used for the surprise gate.
Declared team policy: 1 for PASS, 2 for WARN. Not a physical constant.
Variance used in the gain: R_packet times R_factor.
Belief before this evidence.
Variance of the belief before this evidence and before drift.
Process noise: natural drift allowed for since the last update. Teaching assumption.
Months since the last update of this variable.
Predicted mean just before the update (x minus). Equal to the prior mean because drift has no direction.
Predicted variance just before the update: prior variance plus Q.
Surprise: squared distance of the new value from the prediction, divided by the combined variance.
Surprise limit 3.841 (chi-square, one degree of freedom, 95 %).
True when d2 is above the gate: the model and the evidence disagree.
Named flags raised by this event, for example model_disagreement when d2 is above the gate. Empty when nothing is flagged.
Gain from 0 to 1: how far the twin moves toward the new value.
Belief after the update.
Variance after the update: (1 minus K) times the predicted variance.
Error bar after the update.
New value minus the baseline value.
Combined uncertainty of the change: square root of the two variances added.
Change divided by its uncertainty. Did the value move more than its noise?
Limit for z: 1.96 for the primary variable, 2.394 for secondary ones. Declared before looking.
True for Cho/Cr, the primary variable.
True when the absolute z is above its limit.
Packet the change was measured against.
Plain-language reason for the decision, built from K, z and d2.
The parsed packet, or null when it could not be read.
List of findings, in layer order.
Worst status over all findings: PASS, WARN or FAIL. INFO counts as PASS.
update, update_with_warning or reject, from the status.
The packet value, when it is a valid number. Missing stays missing.
Stated uncertainty as an SD. A 95 % half-width is divided by 1.96.
Uncertainty the twin will use, possibly raised by a consistency rule.
Evidence time in months since baseline.
Variable the packet claims to measure.
Packet identifier.
One-sentence summary of the verdict.
Check layer: parse, schema, semantic, linkage, physics or policy.
Short machine name of the check, for example mrs_snr or source_hash.
PASS, INFO, WARN or FAIL.
Track that owns the check: QE, PM, DS, DT or Shared.
Plain-language reason.
The checked value, when there is one.
Limit the value was compared with, as text.
Extra numbers, for example the recomputed hash or the implied uncertainty.
Variable the prediction is for.
Centre of the expected range: the current belief.
Lower end of the expected range for a clean repeat (95 %).
Upper end of the expected range for a clean repeat (95 %).
Assumed SD of a PASS-quality repeat after re-shimming.
What the prediction assumes, in words.
Epistemic label of the prediction. Always INFERRED.
Candidate next measurement.
Variable the measurement informs.
Scanner time it costs. Zero for offline audits. Teaching value.
Expected SD of the new value, or null when the action tests a bias instead.
Expected quality status of the new measurement.
Causes of the current warning that this measurement removes.
Competing explanations this measurement can tell apart.
Error bar of the twin now.
Expected error bar after the measurement.
Variance removed per scanner minute. Used to rank the candidates.
